# Experiential Avoidance

## Short Definition
Attempts to alter, escape, or suppress unwanted internal experiences even when doing so increases long-term suffering.

## Practical Description
The person tries to control, suppress, or escape thoughts, emotions, memories, or bodily sensations rather than making room for them.

## How It Forms
Often develops through learning that distress can be reduced quickly by escape, distraction, or control.

## How It Is Maintained
Short-term relief reinforces avoidance while valued action, exposure, and emotional processing are narrowed over time. Attempts to avoid or control painful internal experiences may reduce distress briefly, but maintain suffering by narrowing behavior and pulling the person away from valued action.

## Protective Function
Avoidance can reduce immediate distress and protect the person from feared internal states in the short term.

## Long-Term Cost
Life narrows, suffering persists, and the person moves away from what matters.

## Typical Client Signals
- I change the subject when feelings rise.
- I stay busy so I do not have to feel.
- I leave situations when emotion starts.

## Observable Behaviors
Changing topic, staying busy, leaving situations, suppressing emotion, using distraction.

## Typical Thoughts
I cannot handle this feeling. I need to get rid of this now.

## Typical Emotions
Fear, shame, frustration, dread of internal experience.

## Body Responses
Tension, urge to flee, shallow breathing when emotion rises.
